text:
GitHub Copilot's code review can approve pull requests now.

Shipped September 1: Copilot code review now includes an approval assessment, and when an admin turns it on, Copilot's approval counts toward the repository's required-approvals rule. It's off by default. A pushed commit clears it, same as a human reviewer.

What it actually does: it gives you a machine's read on "is this ready" right alongside its comments, and lets a team decide how much weight that read gets.

Why builders should care: review is becoming automatic. Approval -- the actual permission to ship -- is the part still up for a human to configure and grant.

Try this week: turn it on for one low-stakes repo or path. Watch what it flags as ready before you trust it with anything that matters.

The bigger signal: the model was never the hard part. Deciding how much of the yes belongs to a machine is.

Save this for your AI stack.

That's the whole framework if you're building your first monitoring agent:
1. Name one number that actually matters.
2. Set the line where a human needs to know.
3. Let it flag, never act.
4. Keep the yes with a person.
